column3: Uses the same accusatory formula, though Mary is charged with a different grave matter.
Bringing a detailed book offers no meaningful parallel to the abhorrent claim in the focus.
Nearly repeats the formula to condemn an act judged outrageously grave.
Its denial that invoked beings create anything supports the focus passage's rejection of false claims about God.

Condemns the triune claim and reasserts that there is only one God.

Directly states that it is not fitting for God to take a child and grounds creation in His command.

Restates that the offensive assertion is attributing a child to the Merciful.

Makes every being in heaven and earth a servant who comes before the Merciful, excluding divine offspring.

Introduces their false assertion about God as a lie.

Continues the rebuttal of their preference for sons over daughters when attributing offspring to God.
States that God did not take a child and is the One, the Overpowering.
